title: PaneConnection
description: The pane.connection JSON-RPC notification: what a pane's SSH connection is doing, from the moment the pane opens (design §5.6, nocx-oalo1.5.3). Server-initiated and unsolicited, so the same three checks every notification gets apply. It is keyed by paneId and not sessionId because NO SESSION ID EXISTS WHILE OPENING (AD-7): the pane is the renderer's identity from its first frame, and the session id arrives later, in this same notification, when a shell is adopted. connectionEpoch is monotonic per pane and minted at observation, so a receiver can refuse a late observation; it is distinct from sessionEpoch, which names an incarnation, and from livenessEpoch. The transport object is a oneOf discriminated by state: a shape that cannot exist — a stage on a connected connection, a cause on an opening one — is not admitted. `plain` is in the set for the system's own ssh process, which only sees a process and its exit status; no producer in this stage emits it, and the enum is the contract the later carrier fills.

paneId.description: The pane this observation belongs to (AD-7). It is the durable identity the renderer minted, and it is what makes the first observation expressible before any session exists. A receiver routes by this and never by the session id.

connectionId.description: The backend's identity for the connection the pane's shell rides: stable per supervisor entry, and shared by every pane on that connection. It is a derived digest of endpoint, account, credential principal and route, so two panes that share a connection carry one value and two connections to one host under different credentials carry two.

connectionEpoch.description: Monotonic per pane, minted when the observation was made. A receiver drops a notification whose epoch is not greater than the last it applied; a connection that moved on and sent a late observation therefore cannot overwrite the newer state.

instanceId.description: The backend instance that made the observation. It is compared against the value this renderer's backend has always carried, so an observation out of a previous backend instance is refused rather than applied to the current pane.

sessionId.description: The session the pane's shell became, once one is adopted. ABSENT until then, which is the ordinary state during opening: the connection is registered before the shell exists, and that is the whole reason this notification is keyed by pane. When present with instanceId/sessionEpoch it names the incarnation the pane is attached to.

transport.description: The connection's state, in the state machine's own vocabulary (design §5.3). Each branch names exactly the fields its state makes true, so an impossible combination cannot be sent. stateMs is time in this state at observation and the renderer ticks it locally.

oneOf.description: A dial in progress, at one of its stages. This is the state a pane's first observation must arrive in when the shell does not exist yet (design §5.5).

stage.description: Where the dial is: resolve, tcp, ssh-version, key-exchange, sign-in, shell. The list is the design's own; a coarser list is the documented fallback if a stage boundary cannot be observed.

oneOf.description: A step that cannot continue without a person, and the no-progress clock stops here.

person.description: What the answer is for. key-signature is an unanswered agent sign call, which cannot be told from a slow agent; its text says a touch may be needed.

oneOf.description: A usable connection, signed in and answering. plainShells is how many shells a close would end.

plainShells.description: How many shells would end if this connection closed: its own and those of everything dialled through it. It is what makes a reconnect's warning true.

oneOf.description: A connection that has not answered and has not been shown to be gone. Silence alone ends nothing; a connection carrying a plain shell stays here until it answers, the transport errors, or a person presses Reconnect.

stateMs.description: How long the connection has been stalled, at observation. The renderer ticks it from here.

lookAnsweredAt.description: When a look-only dial was answered during this stall, RFC3339 in UTC. It says the HOST accepts new connections while this flow is silent — evidence for a person, never a verdict on the flow. Absent until a look answers.

oneOf.description: A connection whose transport ended while somebody still held it. The next attempt starts here.

attempt.description: How many attempts have been made since it last worked.

oneOf.description: The far side refused in a way no retry changes. Reconnect is the way out.

cause.description: host-key-changed, auth-rejected, no-auth-method, profile-gone. Each needs a person, and nothing retries from here.

oneOf.description: The rest state under policy ask or never: nobody holds the connection any more, or the policy ended it.

cause.description: released is the last holder letting go; silence is the closing policy ending a connection that carried no plain shell.

oneOf.description: The system's own ssh process: nocx sees only the process and its exit status. OpenSSH's 255 covers sign-in and configuration as well as a lost connection, so it reads as 'ssh ended with an error', never as a drop nocx observed. No producer in this stage reaches it; the contract declares it so the carrier that will need no new shape.

quality.description: The newest round-trip measurement and its grade, exactly as session.liveness carries them. ABSENT when nothing measured one: an unanswered probe has no duration, and absent and zero are the same statement — no measurement, never instant. slow is the backend's grade with hysteresis; a reader holding only the milliseconds cannot reproduce it.

attempt.description: The open order's candidates, and nothing else. It says which way of opening the pane was shown and what became of the current candidate; it asserts NOTHING about whether a shell is integrated, because integration stays on lifecycle.changed (ADR-0024). Every member may be 'none' until the open order lands; the object is required so a renderer reads one shape.

reason.description: Why the candidate is where it is, in the backend's own words. Empty when there is nothing to say.

observedAt.description: When the backend observed this, RFC3339 in UTC. The projection's freshness, which is a different question from its order: connectionEpoch decides which of two observations is newer, and this says how old the belief is when it is displayed.
